target_customer: Mobile application developers and mobile site owners
problem: Mobile apps on J2ME were hard to install and impossible to upgrade, limiting adoption.

founders.name: Joshua Wilson
education: MIT, class of 2006 per the YC page
founders.background_notes: YC page describes him as founder of three venture-backed companies without naming them.

technical_complexity.rationale: Building a new language and runtime on top of J2ME across fragmented handsets was hard for two founders.

defensibility.rationale: Developers adopting the language would be locked in, but carriers and handset makers controlled distribution.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: J2ME faded with the smartphone era per sources; no source describes an acquisition of Tsumobi.

market_need_then: The YC description states mobile apps were hard to install and upgrade; no spend or adoption data found.

branding.domain_note: tsumobi.com returned 503 when fetched; history unknown.

brand_strength.rationale: No press about the brand; only a trademark filing for TSUMOBI exists, per Justia.

outcome_analysis: Tsumobi proposed a new language on J2ME so mobile apps could update by visiting a link, and was in the Winter 2007 batch. Directories list it as dead with YC and Draper Richards as investors. J2ME declined with smartphones, so platform timing is a plausible factor, but no source states why it ended and the cause is not public.
notes: The seed round rests on one database (CB Insights); its date 2007-01-22 is probably imprecise for a W07 company and no amount is shown. Draper Richards is also listed by CB Insights only. VCBacked places the company in Cambridge, the YC page says Boston. No dated competitor source found, so the list is empty. The failure factor market_timing_early is an inference. Website returned 503.
